manifest.title: Coupled Frame-Entrenchment Failure Ontology
manifest.description: Self-contained graph-native module for diagnosing and interrupting recursive stabilization of inadequate problem representations in human-LLM inquiry.
scope: model frame capture and externalization failure

relation_vocabulary.definition: links ontology root to a reconstructively central concept
places a concept within a larger process
alters a representation or field of candidates
uses a representation as contextual constraint
converts a contingent artifact into an apparent necessity
feeds back to stabilize a condition
changes an external or representational field
links a failure to a diagnostic criterion
links a failure to a corrective operation
assigns a typed source or status
places rival frames in explicit comparison
states a safeguard or stopping condition

links a case to ontology concepts

links a case to its classification

nodes.label: Coupled Frame-Entrenchment Failure Ontology
nodes.definition: A graph ontology of the coupled human-LLM process by which an inadequate frame can be recursively stabilized, plus disciplined operations for tested frame repair.

nodes.label: Human inquirer
nodes.definition: A human participant whose situated knowledge, ontology, goals, access, and history shape the problem representation communicated to the model.

nodes.label: LLM execution
nodes.definition: A bounded model execution whose continuations are conditioned by the current context, learned structure, instructions, and selection dynamics.

nodes.label: Coupled inquiry system
nodes.definition: The interactional unit formed by the human, model execution, exchanged representations, external actions, and accumulated artifacts.

nodes.label: Target field
nodes.definition: The world, system, evidence, or task about which inquiry is conducted.

nodes.label: Active frame
nodes.definition: The operative arrangement of objects, relations, operations, constraints, evaluation criteria, and candidate alternatives.

nodes.label: Problem representation
nodes.definition: The communicable projection of the target field constituted through the active frame.

nodes.label: Search neighbourhood
nodes.definition: The alternatives treated as sufficiently relevant and expressible to generate or investigate.

nodes.label: Ontological deficit
nodes.definition: An absent, incomplete, conflated, falsely separated, misleveled, or misbounded feature of the active frame.

nodes.label: Better-purpose-fit representation
nodes.definition: An alternative representation that better serves the stated purpose while preserving required invariants and surviving comparison against evidence, constraints, consequences, and rivals.

nodes.label: Corrective structure
nodes.definition: A concept, relation, operation, causal level, unit of analysis, or distinction capable of reorganizing the apparent problem and action space.

nodes.label: Model reconstructibility
nodes.definition: The degree to which corrective structure can plausibly be generated or investigated from model learning plus current evidence; it is not direct evidence of an unspoken internal candidate.

nodes.label: Frame capture
nodes.definition: Model conditioning on the supplied problem representation as the operative world of assistance rather than a revisable hypothesis.

nodes.label: Premise deference
nodes.definition: Treatment of detailed, confident, or effort-laden premises as settled constraints without independent classification.

nodes.label: Local answer optimization
nodes.definition: Selection of an immediately responsive answer inside the active frame without auditing the representation that produced the question.

nodes.label: Corrective externalization failure
nodes.definition: Failure to express reconstructible corrective structure in an inspectable and testable form.

nodes.label: Compensatory structure
nodes.definition: A workaround or artifact created because the active frame lacks a direct representation or operation.

nodes.label: Compensatory structure reification
nodes.definition: Conversion of contingent compensation into an apparent requirement of the task.

nodes.label: Effort-derived constraint credibility
nodes.definition: Increase in apparent constraint authority caused by labor already invested within the frame.

nodes.label: Frame-internal success
nodes.definition: A locally coherent result that is compatible with the frame but may not discriminate it from rivals.

nodes.label: Rhetorical success
nodes.definition: An answer appears coherent or persuasive.

nodes.label: Procedural success
nodes.definition: A next step can be completed.

nodes.label: Symptomatic success
nodes.definition: A visible symptom improves without establishing mechanism.

nodes.label: Metric success
nodes.definition: A chosen measure improves, potentially with unmeasured displacement.

nodes.label: Institutional success
nodes.definition: A procedure or classification becomes adopted and durable.

nodes.label: Causal success
nodes.definition: An intervention affects the operative cause; this is stronger evidence but does not by itself establish exclusivity.

nodes.label: Intervention-induced pseudo-confirmation
nodes.definition: A non-diagnostic intervention changes the outcome and the change is attributed uniquely to the presumed mechanism.

nodes.label: Performative entrenchment
nodes.definition: Frame-generated action modifies the external field so later evidence increasingly resembles the frame.

nodes.label: Search-neighbourhood contraction
nodes.definition: Progressive narrowing of candidate alternatives toward those expressible inside the active frame.

nodes.label: Institutional inscription
nodes.definition: Durable preservation of the frame in policies, code, metrics, forms, roles, training, or other artifacts.

nodes.label: Coupled frame-entrenchment failure
nodes.definition: An emergent failure in which human ontological constraint and frame-conditioned model assistance recursively stabilize an inadequate representation, reify compensation, and suppress tested problem restructuring.

nodes.label: Avoidable burden
nodes.definition: Labor, complexity, error, delay, or risk that a better-purpose-fit representation can reduce without violating required invariants.

nodes.label: Disproportionate compensatory complexity
nodes.definition: A mismatch between a simple required invariant and an elaborate process dominated by decomposition, reconstruction, enumeration, coordination, or symptom repair.

nodes.label: Recursive reinforcement
nodes.definition: Evidence that each interactional cycle increases the authority, elaboration, switching cost, or persistence of the active frame.

nodes.label: Local-success non-uniqueness
nodes.definition: Recognition that local improvement is compatible with multiple causal or representational accounts.

nodes.label: Scale insufficiency
nodes.definition: The framed cause cannot account for the magnitude of the outcome even if perfectly optimized or eliminated.

nodes.label: Frame audit
nodes.definition: A procedure that makes the active representation itself an object of inquiry.

nodes.label: Objective recovery
nodes.definition: Restatement of the required end state independently of the current procedure.

nodes.label: Invariant ledger
nodes.definition: Explicit list of what an alternative preserves, loses, assumes, requires verification of, and introduces.

nodes.label: Constraint provenance classification
nodes.definition: Typing constraints by source and warrant rather than treating all stated limits as equivalent.

nodes.label: Logical constraint
nodes.definition: A condition required by consistency, identity, or formal entailment.

nodes.label: Physical constraint
nodes.definition: A condition imposed by material or causal possibility.

nodes.label: Empirical constraint
nodes.definition: A condition supported by observation or measurement under declared scope.

nodes.label: Technical constraint
nodes.definition: A condition imposed by an implemented system, interface, version, or architecture.

nodes.label: Permission constraint
nodes.definition: A condition imposed by access control or authority.

nodes.label: Legal constraint
nodes.definition: A condition imposed by applicable law or regulation.

nodes.label: Safety constraint
nodes.definition: A condition required to control asymmetric harm.

nodes.label: Organizational constraint
nodes.definition: A condition imposed by roles, governance, capacity, or institutional process.

nodes.label: Conventional constraint
nodes.definition: A condition maintained by standard practice or interoperability convention.

nodes.label: Inherited assumption
nodes.definition: A premise carried forward from prior practice without current independent warrant.

nodes.label: Adjacent-ontology search
nodes.definition: Search across neighbouring disciplines, scales, units of analysis, and standard primitives for structures matching the recovered invariant.

nodes.label: Rival-frame generation
nodes.definition: Construction of multiple plausible representations that preserve the objective while changing decomposition, cause, operation set, or unit of analysis.

nodes.label: Discriminating test
nodes.definition: A test designed to produce meaningfully different expectations under rival frames.

nodes.label: Scale sufficiency test
nodes.definition: Comparison of the maximum effect available to the framed cause with the magnitude of the observed outcome.

nodes.label: Figure-ground reversal
nodes.definition: Foregrounding backgrounded or excluded structure that could reorganize the current figure.

nodes.label: Corrective externalization
nodes.definition: Expression of candidate corrective structure as a qualified, testable alternative rather than as hidden certainty.

nodes.label: Ontological escape
nodes.definition: Controlled transition to a tested better-purpose-fit representation.

nodes.label: Genuine irreducible complexity
nodes.definition: Complexity that persists after independent reformulation because required constraints remain operative.

nodes.label: Model knowledge absence
nodes.definition: The model lacks and cannot plausibly reconstruct the corrective structure from available evidence.

nodes.label: Deliberate constraint acceptance
nodes.definition: An expensive or limited path intentionally serves the actual objective.

nodes.label: Temporary scaffolding
nodes.definition: A knowingly incomplete and revisable representation used for bounded action.

nodes.label: Emergency priority
nodes.definition: Immediate asymmetric risk requires safe action before exploratory reframing.

nodes.label: Fixed-frame task
nodes.definition: The task requires compliance, faithful reproduction, or work inside an explicitly fixed representation.

nodes.label: Empirically rejected alternative
nodes.definition: A candidate has already failed a coherent test under relevant conditions.

nodes.label: Ontological plurality
nodes.definition: Multiple representations are legitimate for different purposes, scales, or preservation policies.

nodes.label: Value conflict
nodes.definition: The apparent problem includes irreducibly normative disagreement not removable by technical optimization.

nodes.label: Underdetermination
nodes.definition: Available evidence supports several live interpretations without selecting one.

nodes.label: Over-reframing
nodes.definition: Unwarranted replacement of a frame by novelty or elegance while dropping evidence, purpose, or real constraints.

nodes.label: The coupled system is the diagnostic unit
nodes.definition: The failure is constituted by recursive interaction among human framing, model conditioning, external action, and accumulated artifacts; it is not located wholly in either participant.

nodes.label: Local success does not uniquely validate a frame
nodes.definition: Coherent or useful results inside a frame can occur under several rival causal or representational accounts.

nodes.label: Compensation can be mistaken for necessity
nodes.definition: A workaround generated by a representational gap can become reified as part of the problem itself.

nodes.label: Effort can reinforce the frame that generated it
nodes.definition: Labor within a frame can increase its credibility to both human and model even when the labor is avoidable.

nodes.label: A frame can help create its own evidence
nodes.definition: Actions generated under a frame can modify the external field and produce later observations interpreted as confirmation.

nodes.label: Correction targets the problem representation
nodes.definition: The decisive transition is often from one problem representation to another, not merely from one answer to a better answer.

nodes.label: Adequacy is purpose-relative and constrained
nodes.definition: A corrected representation is better only relative to purpose, evidence, required invariants, real constraints, consequences, and comparison with rivals.

nodes.label: Disproportionate complexity is a signal, not proof
nodes.definition: Compensatory complexity warrants a frame audit but does not establish that a simpler valid alternative exists.

nodes.label: Model reconstructibility is not observed internal activation
nodes.definition: The ability to generate corrective structure under some prompting does not prove that a fully formed unspoken answer was present in a prior execution.

nodes.label: Reframing has stopping conditions
nodes.definition: The model should preserve an operative frame when emergency, compliance, reproducibility, tested rejection, underdetermination, value conflict, or genuine constraints make reframing unsafe or inapposite.
